thread:
maria: hey team — seeing intermittent 401s in CI when calling Redwood API. Local dev and prod envs are fine, only failing on the shared runners. API_KEY is stored as a secret. Any quick checks?
aj: are you constructing the Basic header correctly? it should be base64(<api_key>:), so include the trailing colon.
maria: doing this in the job: `TOKEN=$(echo $API_KEY | base64)` then `curl -H \"Authorization: Basic $TOKEN\" ...`
leo: echo will add a newline. on some shells/runner wrappers that becomes part of the string. also watch for CR (\r) if the secret was copied from Windows. that breaks the header.
sam: simple repro: `echo 'key123' | xxd` -> shows `0a` at the end. try `echo -n` or `printf '%s'`.
maria: ugh — GitLab masks the secret so i couldn't see trailing chars. how to safely do this across sh / bash in CI?
aj: CI-agnostic pattern: `API_B64=$(printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | tr -d '\r' | openssl base64 -A)` — `tr -d '\r'` removes CR, `-A` keeps it on one line. then use `-H \"Authorization: Basic $API_B64\"`.
leo: if you suspect NUL (\x00) bytes, inspect with `printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | od -An -t x1` — NUL appears as `00`. some secret backends pad with nulls. also strip them with `tr -d '\000'` or `tr -d '\0'`.
maria: can you paste a small robust snippet i can drop into our job?
sam: sure — drop this in your script:
```
# robust header builder (bash/sh)
CLEAN=$(printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | tr -d '\r\000')
AUTH=$(printf '%s' "$CLEAN" | openssl base64 -A)
# note: we intentionally base64 the key alone if server expects key: then append ':' before base64
# if Redwood expects key:, use: printf '%s:' "$CLEAN" | openssl base64 -A
curl -H "Authorization: Basic $AUTH" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
aj: quick note: some base64 binaries insert newlines; `base64 -w0` on GNU or `openssl base64 -A` are portable ways to keep a single line. also prefer `printf` over `echo` for portability.
leo: windows/pwsh tip for completeness:
```
# pwsh
$raw = (Get-Content -Raw -Path env:API_KEY) -replace '\r|\x00',''
$bytes = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($raw + ':')
$auth = [Convert]::ToBase64String($bytes)
# then header: Authorization: Basic $auth
```
maria: thanks all — found a hidden NUL appended by our secret injector. trimmed it in the job with `tr -d '\000'` and switched to `openssl base64 -A`. CI now returns 200s consistently :tada:
ci-bot: pipeline #8421 succeeded for branch fix/ci-secret-trim (runtime: 45s)
maria: closing — appreciate the quick help!
